safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts note lip swelling but do not include the duration ('past 1 hour') or an equivalent timeframe.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the duration of lip swelling removes an important timeline detail for assessing acuity and progression of a suspected allergic reaction/anaphylaxis. While not typically changing first-line emergency management, it can impair triage, handoff, and reassessment of symptom trajectory.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold includes throat closing sensation; generated facts mention difficulty breathing/chest tightness but not throat closing or throat swelling.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: A sensation of throat closing is a key red-flag feature suggestive of impending airway compromise in anaphylaxis; omitting it can lead to underestimation of severity and less urgent escalation in other settings or during handoff. This has meaningful potential for harm if it delays emergency treatment.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states the patient appeared to have breathing difficulties during the consultation (clinician observation); generated facts only list symptoms/ROS without documenting this observed finding.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document observed breathing difficulty removes an objective severity marker that can support urgency, monitoring intensity, and downstream clinical decisions during handoff. Because patient-reported dyspnea is still documented, the incremental harm is typically limited to reduced clarity and potentially extra monitoring.
